title: Simplification (P22 reversed): delete Peri-LN's branch-output LayerNorms from all six blocks and the MTP block, so every block runs the fork's plain pre-LN forward, on the 191-claude incumbent (9,548,544 params; -5 lines)
description: Idea ID: P22 reversed (107-claude's Peri-LN), the 'Peri-LN's extra branch-output norms' candidate in program.md's simplify-the-incumbent list and its 'fewer norms' speed lead: PeriLNBlock loses ln_attn_out, ln_mlp_out and its forward override, so the six trunk blocks and the pretraining-only MTP block run the fork Block's forward x + attn(ln1(x)), x + fc2(gelu(fc1(ln2(x)))); model width, heads, ALiBi/NoPE split, optimizers, schedule, init rule, data order, MTP and handoff are 191-claude's. Peri-LN's one A/B (107: +7.3, paired +45/-23/0, carried by one seed's better start) was noise-sized on a 4.8M RoPE model without MTP or token batches, so the 14 extra LayerNorms may be dead weight for expert iteration, and removing them frees step time for more pretraining steps.
hypothesis: Peri-LN normalizes every residual write to unit RMS times a learned gain; its benefit in Kim et al. (2025) is stability at scale (no massive activations, no variance growth over depth). Here the model is 6 blocks deep, hidden matrices are trained by Muon (orthogonalized, spectral-norm-bounded steps with lr-coupled decoupled decay 0.1) and every branch input is still LayerNormed, so residual growth over 6 blocks is bounded and the output norms mostly re-parametrize branch scale: with them, Muon's decay on proj/fc2 cannot shrink a write (only the AdamW-decayed output gains can); without them, decay and the orthogonal init (element std 0.02) set the scale as in the pre-107 Lean incumbents. Prediction: pretraining fits at least as well (107 measured slightly WORSE final val loss with Peri-LN, 0.0822-0.0836 vs 0.0806-0.0820), steps rise ~4-9% (107 measured the 12 output norms at ~10% of steps in eager torch 2.4; per-block compile fuses part of that cost), and the RL start and final metric are statistically unchanged. Counter-hypothesis this tests: with unnormalized writes the frozen RL fine-tune (AdamW lr 3e-4, 600 steps per round) moves proj/fc2 writes directly instead of through a scale-free LayerNorm, so RL could drift or destabilize and extrapolate worse to >= 7-line targets; a 3-seed mean below 665 or round-4 RL-solved below 1,140 on 2+ seeds would support that. Decision rule fixed now, the same simplification rule 189-fable, 190-claude and 191-claude registered: keep if the 3-seed mean is >= 680.3 (strictly above 191's 683.67 or within 3.3 of it, program.md's '~0 with less code' rule; this removes 5 lines and 14 LayerNorms); below 680.3 discard. If the other agent keeps a file first, record.py's rule applies.
expected_delta: -30 to +20 vs 191's 683.67 (central -4); keep needs a 3-seed mean >= 680.3 (rule in the hypothesis). Pretraining 5,350-5,950 steps in 300 s per seed (central 5,650; 191: 5,362/5,298/5,220; estimated, the bench found no A40), ~4.8-5.3 epochs; final val loss 0.075-0.095, last train loss 0.035-0.06; held-out greedy after pretraining 0.95-0.98 (191: 0.971/0.972/0.959); round-1 RL targets solved 300-800 (noisy: 190/191 ranged 225-779); round-4 RL-solved 1,130-1,200 (191: 1,189/1,160/1,142); handoff n_params 9,548,544 exactly; RL sampling within 10% of 191's rate (two fewer LayerNorms per block per token); totals 1,650-2,100 s. Falsifiers: mean steps below 5,350 (the compiled output norms cost less than 1%); a mean below 665 says Peri-LN is still worth >= 19 on this recipe.

arch.type: gpt (fork model.py) ALiBiGPT with hybrid ALiBi/NoPE heads; blocks are the fork Block (pre-LN forward inherited) with fc1/fc2 replaced by Linear(D, D_FF)/Linear(D_FF, D), D_FF = 1280; the class keeps the historical name PeriLNBlock (compile_dev.py builds it) but has no branch-output LayerNorms
arch.pos: hybrid alibi/nope (unchanged from 115-fable): no rotation of q/k in any block; additive per-head bias -slope_h * (query position - key position) on the scaled attention logits via SDPA attn_mask, slopes 2^(-8h/4) = 1/4, 1/16, 1/64, 1/256 for heads 1..4 (Press et al. 2021 standard set for 4 heads) and 0 for heads 5..8 (bias identically 0 except -inf for masked/future keys, i.e. NoPE heads); same slope table in every block; -inf for masked/future keys
arch.norm: layernorm, pre-LN only: the fork Block's ln1/ln2 on the attention and MLP branch inputs and ln_f before the head. Removed: Peri-LN's ln_attn_out/ln_mlp_out on the branch outputs (107-claude) in all six trunk blocks and in the MTP block
arch.change: vs 191-claude: PeriLNBlock's ln_attn_out, ln_mlp_out and forward override are deleted (the class now inherits the fork Block.forward: x = x + attn(ln1(x)); x = x + fc2(gelu(fc1(ln2(x))))), in the six trunk blocks and the MTP block alike; two stale comments updated. Everything else, including ALiBi attention, KV-cache code, MTP loss, optimizers, schedule, init, data order and handoff, is 191-claude's
arch.n_params_detail: model: 9,548,544 (CPU check with fork 51604b3, vocab 107: model.n_params() and sum(numel) agree); per block 1,577,600 = qkv 443,520 + proj 147,840 + fc1 492,800 + fc2 491,904 + 2 LayerNorms 1,536 (191: 1,579,136 with 4 LayerNorms), x6 = 9,465,600; emb + head 82,176; ln_f 768. -9,216 vs 191. MTP module (pretraining only, never registered on the model, dropped at handoff): 1,874,048 (191: 1,875,584)
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: ALiBiGPT(vocab, 6, 384, 8) from this pretrain.py with PeriLNBlock blocks (fork Block forward, d_ff 1280, no output LayerNorms), then load state; the MTP module is not saved and not needed for inference
arch.kv_cache: code unchanged (ALiBi attn override with the fork's preallocated cache; caches[0] holds key positions); CPU check after a 25 s CPU pretrain with fork 51604b3: prefill 10 tokens then 75 single-token cached steps vs one full forward, max abs logit diff 2.9e-6 (T 85); fork sample.generate_ids runs end to end

tokenizer.source: fork 51604b3 lean_tok.LeanTokenizer('lean_seq') via tokenizer.make_tokenizer; Lean 4 have-chain text, names n1..n64 numbered by first appearance

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale) with Polar Express orthogonalization on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight; AdamW on embeddings, biases and LayerNorms; the MTP module's five 2D matrices (block qkv split into Q/K/V, block proj, fc1, fc2, and the (384,768) input proj) join Muon and its LayerNorms/biases join AdamW (unchanged from 151/191)
optimizer.schedule: cosine over wall-clock from step 1, no warmup: lr = 1e-3 * (0.3 + 0.35 * (1 + cos(pi * frac))), frac = elapsed / budget (setup and per-block compile included, so the first step runs at ~0.99 x peak after ~30-35 s), ending at 0.3 x peak; Muon lr = 0.01 * lr / 1e-3 and its decoupled decay follow the same factor. Removed: 186's 200-step linear warmup (lr = 1e-3 * step / 200 for step < 200)

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / D) with D = 384 per orthogonalized matrix (RMS-matched, Moonshot convention with its 0.2 constant folded into MUON_LR): Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 (1280,384) and fc2 (384,1280) sqrt(1280/384) = 1.83, head (107,384) 1, MTP proj (384,768) sqrt(2); MUON_LR 0.01 unchanged
muon.schedule: same cosine fraction as AdamW from step 1, no warmup (floor 0.3, unchanged); muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: 6 x (qkv.weight (1152,384) split into Q/K/V, proj, fc1, fc2) plus head.weight, plus the MTP module's 5 matrices: 30 Muon matrices as in 148/151 (CPU check: muon_step runs over all 30)
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: unchanged: each QKV update reshaped to (3,384,384), orthogonalized per role; fc1 (1280,384) is not (3D, D) so it is orthogonalized whole
muon.coefficients_note: per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; values as in modded-nanogpt, num_iters=5, safety factor 2e-2, cushion 2) replace Keller Jordan's fixed (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) used five times. Same five iterations (two matmuls each on the Gram side plus one), same bf16 precision, same transpose/QKV-split/shape-scale handling.
muon.normalization: update / (Frobenius norm * 1.02 + 1e-6) (Polar Express safety factor) instead of update / (Frobenius norm + 1e-7)
muon.local_check: CPU check (float64 scalar map over sigma in [1e-3,1]): output singular values in [0.847,1.141] vs fixed quintic [0.471,1.202]; for sigma>=3e-3 [0.859,1.141] vs [0.682,1.202]. bf16 torch on random (256,256)/(1024,256)/(99,256) matrices: median singular value 0.94/0.95/1.02 vs 0.75/0.77/0.77, update RMS +14%/+14%/+19%.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (ln1, ln2 per block, ln_f; the MTP module's ln_h, ln_e and its block's ln1/ln2); head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW. 191's ln_attn_out/ln_mlp_out gains and biases no longer exist
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1, so Muon per-step shrinkage lr*0.1 is ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 (peak 1e-3 per step), applied to all 25 trunk/head Muon matrices (+5 MTP); AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3. Note: without output LayerNorms, Muon decay on proj/fc2 again shrinks each branch's residual write directly (as before 107); under 191's Peri-LN it only re-parametrized them
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 over model.parameters() + the MTP module's parameters, before both optimizers (unchanged)
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; the MTP module and both pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW on model.parameters()
optimizer.parameters: 24 trunk hidden matrices + head.weight, plus the MTP module's qkv (split), proj, fc1, fc2 and input proj (384,768): 30 Muon matrices during pretraining; the handoff model's parameters are 9,557,760

batch.padding: to max len in batch (the batch's last, longest record); mean padded tokens per step ~18.3k of which ~18.3k real (>99% fill), vs the incumbent's ~51-54k padded slots for ~17.3k real tokens
batch.change: fairseq-style max-tokens batching replaces fixed 128 random records per step: per epoch, randperm the training records (GPU generator, seed), stable-argsort by total length so equal lengths stay shuffled, cut greedily into consecutive runs with count * max_len <= 18,432, then shuffle the run order with random.Random(seed). Loss is the same per-token mean over the batch's proof tokens; the shift augmentation, Muon/AdamW updates, clip and wall-clock cosine are unchanged (the 200-step warmup those runs had is removed in 191, see optimizer.schedule). The val slice still uses fixed chunks of 128.
batch.size_note: variable: a run of length-sorted records with count * padded_length <= TOK_BUDGET = 18,432 tokens (128 x 144); on a synthetic length distribution matching mean ~135 / max 537 that is 33..921 records per batch, mean ~136, so ~1,130 batches per epoch (incumbent: 128 fixed, ~1,204 per epoch)

data.augmentation: random name start offset (lean_seq; same vectorised shift as abs over the n1..n64 name tokens)
data.order: shuffle at the record level each epoch, then length-homogeneous batches in shuffled order (data-order change: within a step all records have similar total length; across steps lengths are interleaved at random)

config.compile: per-block torch.compile(dynamic=True), coalesce_tiling_analysis off, undone at handoff; Muon step as one CUDA graph; fused AdamW; batch max length from host
config.init: unchanged rule from 148/151/191: fork _init (normal 0.02 embedding/readout, zero biases), orthogonal_ on every 2D block and MTP parameter with gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols)), so element std stays 0.02 at width 384; LayerNorm gain 1, bias 0

loss.main: the fork's loss_on: next-token cross-entropy on proof-token positions (unchanged; val_loss and the recorded train_loss/last_loss use this term only, so they stay comparable with 129)
loss.mtp: DeepSeek-V3 (2024) sequential multi-token prediction, depth 1 (Gloeckle et al. 2024 style shared head): z_t = proj(cat(LN(h_t), LN(emb(x_{t+1})))) for t in 0..T-3, one pre-LN causal block (the same fork Block forward as the trunk, no output LayerNorms) over z with the same ALiBi/NoPE bias sliced to T-2 positions, then the model's ln_f and head predict x_{t+2}; cross-entropy masked to proof-token targets (m[:, 2:]), mean over those positions (unchanged from 191 except the block's norms)
loss.total: main + MTP_WEIGHT * mtp with MTP_WEIGHT = 0.3 constant over the whole budget (DeepSeek-V3's early-training value); curve points also record the mean recent mtp loss as mtp_loss
loss.leakage_check: CPU check: perturbing token x[7] changes the MTP block's outputs only at positions 6..9 (which read emb(x[7]) or later), never at position 5 whose target is x[7]

config.bench: not run: bench_pretrain.py --secs 60 waited 530 s at 09:56-10:05 BST (14 'no NVIDIA A40 capacity' attempts), then was interrupted; no pod was created. Step count estimated from 107's measured cost of the same 12 output LayerNorms (~10% of steps, eager torch 2.4, width 256), discounted for per-block compile fusion; make -C code check clean; CPU smoke run (25 s, 3 steps) and cached-decode check pass
config.init_rng: identical to 191's per seed: LayerNorm construction draws no random numbers (ones/zeros), so deleting two per block leaves the fork _init and orthogonal_ draws, data order and shift augmentation draws seed-for-seed equal to 191; only the forward differs
